sentences.text: Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 16666 of 2023

Applicant :- Niraj Kumar
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Kamaleshwari Prasad Kushwaha,Raj Nath Bhakta
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri. Kamaleshwari Prasad Kushwaha, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The present application has been filed on behalf of applicant in Case Crime No. 792 of 2021 under Sections328, 376, 506 of IPC and Section 66E, 67A Information Technology (Amendment) Act 2008, Police Station Chakeri, District Kanpur Nagar with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
3. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is further submitted that the victim is major girl and she was a consenting party she established physical relation with the applicant.

It is next submitted that the victim refused for her medication examination and victim has always demand money from the applicant when the application denied to pay the money the present false F.I.R. has been lodged against the applicant.
Lastly it is submitted that applicant languishing in jail since 25.12.2022 having no criminal history and in case, he is released on bail he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

Niraj Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113398672/

entities.text: Niraj Kumar vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned Additional Government Advocate has opposed the prayer for grant of bail and argued that as per C.D.R. report it has been corroborated that the number of which the applicant was sending obscene material belongs to the applicant.

It is also submitted that as per surveillance report the mobile number 96196096 and 8595748952 were used by the applicant in a mobile set which indicate that applicant sent message to the victim by these numbers.

5. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of allegations and gravity of offence, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the opinion that no case for grant of bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby rejected.
6. Any observation made above shall not be treated as any finding on the merit and shall not prejudice the trial.
